html:
Baalbek, called Heliopolis by the Greeks and Romans, is a town in the Bekaa valley of Lebanon with some of the largest Roman temples ever built, raised over about two centuries from the time of Augustus.

The temple of Jupiter stood on a platform that includes some of the largest stones ever cut, each weighing several hundred tonnes. Its six standing columns are among the tallest of the Roman world. The temple of Bacchus nearby is one of the best preserved.

Later the site became a fortress under Arab rulers. It became a World Heritage Site in 1984, and since 1956 has been the stage of the Baalbeck Festival. Baalbek is also a stronghold of Hezbollah. See also the Roman Empire and Lebanon.
sum: Baalbek, called Heliopolis by the Greeks and Romans, is a town in the Bekaa valley of Lebanon with some of the largest Roman temples ever built, raised over about two centuries from the time of Augustus.
